required_adapter_guards: Preserve existing v1 canonical bytes, digest, feature output and unsupported behavior; a parallel side table or single traversal must retain module-wide lexical binder allocation and identity scope, including function parameters. Never reconstruct identity from names.

Treat command formula, each function body, and each fact as separate named-by-anonymous-path roots in the same entire anonymous module context. No call inlining; preserve whole calls, binders, lets, temporal and unsupported subtrees as opaque atoms and do not rewrite descendants.

Opaque atom payload is exact anonymous structure and sort, with resolved slot identities and no user names, source text or hashes as sole identity. Preserve a stable complete atom inventory through extraction even if atoms disappear.

Derive schema from resolved Alloy Type.fold as the complete set of ordered nominal primitive signature tuples, with anonymous registered signature or builtin identities, sorted and deduplicated deterministically; reject unmappable or ambiguous types. Compare full exact operand and result schemas, including empty relations, at every relational operator and rule instance.

The Lean single-Tuple relation model proves abstract fixed-carrier laws, not Alloy parser correspondence, schema extraction, Java implementation refinement or contextual correctness of plugging roots back into a module. Expose these as trusted assumptions and test obligations.
required_tests: Byte-for-byte golden tests of v1 structural output, digest and features, including unsupported behavior and multiple roots.
Alpha-renamed globals and binders yield identical complete typed inputs; shadowed and separate parameter identities remain distinct and no raw labels enter payloads.
Functions, facts and command roots stay separately identified with the full module context; call bodies and descendants of opaque binder/call nodes never change.

Same arity distinct nominal signatures, multi-alternative folded types, column permutations, builtin identities and mismatched result types fail relational gating; relation plus/minus never confuse integer or override variants.
Adversarial opaque subtree, schema, context, root path, inventory and output tampering is rejected by independent proof replay; budget stops never imply saturation or complete normalization.
integration_plan: Extend the existing module/expression traversal with an optional immutable per-occurrence capture sink, recording resolved node, root path, captured canonical subtree and lexical state without changing constructor trees or traversal order.

Add a separate child-side adapter that lowers each captured function body, fact and command formula using occurrence records and resolved types; stop at opaque nodes, never revisit descendants, and fail closed on unresolved or unsupported schemas.

Canonicalize each complete Type.fold schema to sorted unique ordered tuples of anonymous nominal slots or builtins. Require exact operand and result schemas for relational lowering; reject unknown identities and ambiguous forms.

Build a stable exact atom inventory before engine invocation; retain the complete anonymous module and exact occurrence path in every island context. Keep implementation outside the v1 artifact and feature encoding pipeline.
Run v1 byte/digest/vector golden tests and adversarial shared-AST, shadowing, alpha-renaming, opaque boundary, multi-alternative schema and per-root isolation tests.
revision_2_disposition: Resolved: occurrence and structural path capture explicitly precludes object-identity cache, identifies the exact root occurrence, and rejects mismatched AST/subtree pairs.
Resolved: full typed anonymous atom encodings are sorted and deduplicated before rewrites, with checker-enforced ordered membership and trusted original inventory binding.
Review is limited to adapter contract precision; no formal closure, parser correspondence or implementation correctness is asserted.
